question: When the AbortSignal is already aborted, does each adapter fail before any request leaves the process with an identifiable abort error, and when a stream is aborted mid-flight does iteration terminate promptly, with wire evidence that the upstream request was cut short?
finding: Pre-dispatch (signal already aborted): @google/genai threw nothing (returned) (abort-distinguishable=false, HTTP none, requests that left the process: yes); the AI SDK threw AbortError (abort-distinguishable=true, HTTP none, requests that left the process: no). Mid-stream: genai saw 1 chunk(s) and threw AbortError in 0ms; the AI SDK saw 1 chunk(s) and threw AbortError in 0ms. On the wire, genai relayCompleted=true, clientDisconnected=false, upstreamCutShort=false; the AI SDK relayCompleted=true, clientDisconnected=false, upstreamCutShort=false. The proxy did not observe a downstream disconnect for this run, so the wire cannot confirm upstream cancellation there; what is recorded is iteration terminating promptly after the abort. The AI SDK short-circuits an already-aborted signal on its own, at the fetch level, while @google/genai lets the call go out regardless. That is the behavior geminiAbort.throwIfAborted compensates for, though note its narrow use today: it is called from the server-tool and auth paths (GeminiProvider.resolveAuthWithAbortCheck and geminiServerTools), not from the ordinary chat generation path this probe exercises.
